title: The future of Slip into Ruby

posts.author: Trihan
posts.body:
So unfortunately, the Slip into Ruby articles were on rpgmaker.net, which basically no longer exists, at least for now. I started the series on a machine I no longer have ready access to, and that's where all the original files were stored, so I don't have backups either. But given how many people the series has helped over the years, I'm loath to allow it to die, so I'm planning to take the only option available to me: remake it, but posted somewhere I can easily restore or repost it.
With that in mind, here's your chance to make it better! If you've ever read any of the series, is there anything you think didn't work so well? Anything about it you'd change? I'm willing to take another stab at doing them in video format, which will allow me to more easily jump between classes and demonstrate in the engine how some things work, but the feedback on that back in the day was that the preference was having it written, so I'm not sure on that one.

posts.body:
Trihan said:
Anything about it you'd change? I'm willing to take another stab at doing them in video format, which will allow me to more easily jump between classes and demonstrate in the engine how some things work
Click to expand...
I have some work colleagues that would love to have this in videos. They want everything in videos!
Some people learn and will prefer videos all the time. I find the video to be ok for the first time learning, after that I would prefer writing with images..
I don't think I have any suggestions about any of your tutorials, except maybe add on a sampling of advanced projects. Or explaining why some scripts are designed the way they are. Finding compatibility resolutions.
Although I admit I have not read your tutorials front to back. I often look for info when I need that specific info. Otherwise thanks for making an effort to restore this information.
